e-12659.knowledge_point: Finding the Maximum Value Given a Canonical Form on the Unit Sphere
e-12659.problem: Find the maximum value of $Q(\mathbf{x})=2x_1^2 - 5x_2^2 +3x_3^2$ given that $\| \mathbf{x} \| =1.$
e-12659.worked_solution:
First, notice that $x_1^2 \geq 0$ and $x_2^2 \geq 0.$ So, we have that 

$$
2x_1^2 \leq 3x_1^2, \qquad -5x_2^2 \leq 3x_2^2.
$$

As a result, 

$$
\begin{aligned}Q(x) & =2{x}_{1}^{2}-5{x}_{2}^{2}+3{x}_{3}^{2} \\  & \le 3{x}_{1}^{2}+3{x}_{2}^{2}+3{x}_{3}^{2} \\  & =3({x}_{1}^{2}+{x}_{2}^{2}+{x}_{3}^{2}).\end{aligned}
$$

Now, recall that $\| \mathbf{x} \| = 1$ is equivalent to $x_1^2 + x_2^2 + x_3^2 =1.$ So, 

$$
\begin{aligned}3({x}_{1}^{2}+{x}_{2}^{2}+{x}_{3}^{2})=3(1)=3,\end{aligned}
$$

and, in turn, $Q(\mathbf{x}) \leq 3.$

So, the value of $Q(\mathbf{x})$ can be no greater than $3.$ But before we conclude that $3$ is the maximum, we need to find a vector such that $Q(\mathbf{x}) = 3.$

Notice that when ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14070559/assets/1986d7b40e318db91ac16ba9540ec704fd6221ac295dec66540c190a090a1463.png) we get

$$
\begin{aligned}Q(x) & =2{x}_{1}^{2}-5{x}_{2}^{2}+3{x}_{3}^{2} \\  & =2(0)^{2}-5(0)^{2}+3(1)^{2} \\  & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, given that $\| \mathbf{x} \| =1,$ the maximum value of $Q(\mathbf{x})$ is equal to $3.$

e-12660.knowledge_point: Finding the Minimum Value Given a Canonical Form on the Unit Sphere
e-12660.problem: Find the minimum value of $Q(\mathbf{x})=5x_1^2 - 4x_2^2 - 6x_3^2$ given that $\| \mathbf{x} \| =1.$
e-12660.worked_solution:
First, notice that $x_1^2 \geq 0$ and $x_2^2 \geq 0.$ So, we have that

$$
5x_1^2 \geq -6x_1^2, \qquad -4x_2^2 \geq -6x_2^2.
$$

As a result, 

$$
\begin{aligned}Q(x) & =5{x}_{1}^{2}-4{x}_{2}^{2}-6{x}_{3}^{2} \\  & \ge -6{x}_{1}^{2}-6{x}_{2}^{2}-6{x}_{3}^{2} \\  & =-6({x}_{1}^{2}+{x}_{2}^{2}+{x}_{3}^{2}).\end{aligned}
$$

Now, recall that $\| \mathbf{x} \| = 1$ is equivalent to $x_1^2 + x_2^2 + x_3^2 =1.$ So, 

$$
\begin{aligned}-6({x}_{1}^{2}+{x}_{2}^{2}+{x}_{3}^{2})=-6(1)=-6.\end{aligned}
$$

and, in turn, $Q(\mathbf{x}) \geq -6.$

So, the value of $Q(\mathbf{x})$ can be no smaller than $-6.$ But before we conclude that $-6$ is the minimum, we need to find a vector such that $Q(\mathbf{x}) = -6.$

Notice that when ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14070559/assets/d509eb79bc8d9a96b60922166e49d0225eac7a99d2614859c31af15199d4d47c.png) we get

$$
\begin{aligned}Q(x) & =5{x}_{1}^{2}-4{x}_{2}^{2}-6{x}_{3}^{2} \\  & =5(0)^{2}-4(0)^{2}-6(1)^{2} \\  & =-6.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, given that $\| \mathbf{x} \| =1,$ the minimum value of $Q(\mathbf{x})$ is equal to $-6.$

e-12661.knowledge_point: Finding the Maximum and Minimum Values of a Quadratic Form on the Unit Sphere
e-12661.problem: Find the minimum value of $Q(\mathbf{x})=x_1^2-2x_2^2-2x_3^2+2x_2x_3$  given that $\| \mathbf{x} \| = 1.$
e-12661.worked_solution:
Let $A$ be the matrix corresponding to our quadratic form. Recall that: 

- The maximum value of $Q(\mathbf{x}),$ when $\| \mathbf{x} \|=1,$ is equal to the largest eigenvalue of $A{:}$

$$
\max \{ Q(\mathbf{x}) \: | \:  \| \mathbf{x} \| = 1 \} = \lambda_{\textrm{max}}
$$

- The minimum value of $Q(\mathbf{x}),$ when $\| \mathbf{x} \|=1,$ is equal to the smallest eigenvalue of $A{:}$

$$
\min \{ Q(\mathbf{x}) \: | \:  \| \mathbf{x} \| = 1 \} = \lambda_{\textrm{min}}
$$

First, we write down the matrix of our quadratic form:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14070559/assets/d7716e2c2924212e880275dd674d4a951daf66ac41e5a888a57acb6be686118f.png)

Now, we need to calculate the eigenvalues of the matrix $A\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}|A-\lambda I| & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}1-\lambda  & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -2-\lambda  & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & -2-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (1-\lambda )|\begin{aligned}-2-\lambda  & 1 \\ 1 & -2-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (1-\lambda )((-2-\lambda )(-2-\lambda )-1) & =0 \\ (1-\lambda )({\lambda }^{2}+4\lambda +3) & =0 \\ (1-\lambda )(\lambda +3)(\lambda +1) & =0 \\ \lambda  & =1,\,-1,\,-3\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\min \{ Q(\mathbf{x}) \: | \:  \| \mathbf{x} \| = 1 \} = -3.
$$

content.problem: Find the maximum value of $Q(x)=5{x}_{1}^{2}+8{x}_{2}^{2}$ given that $‖x‖=1.$
content.worked_solution:
First, notice that ${x}_{1}^{2}\ge 0.$ So, we have that

$$
5{x}_{1}^{2}\le 8{x}_{1}^{2}.
$$

As a result, 

$$
\begin{aligned}Q(x) & =5{x}_{1}^{2}+8{x}_{2}^{2} \\  & \le 8{x}_{1}^{2}+8{x}_{2}^{2} \\  & =8({x}_{1}^{2}+{x}_{2}^{2}).\end{aligned}
$$

Now, recall that $‖x‖=1$ is equivalent to ${x}_{1}^{2}+{x}_{2}^{2}=1.$ So, 

$$
\begin{aligned}8({x}_{1}^{2}+{x}_{2}^{2})=8(1)=8.\end{aligned}
$$

and, in turn, $Q(x)\le 8.$

So, the value of $Q(x)$ can be no greater than $8.$ But before we conclude that $8$ is the maximum, we need to find a vector such that $Q(x)=8.$

Notice that when  $x={[\begin{aligned}0 & 1\end{aligned}]}^{T},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}Q(x) & =5{x}_{1}^{2}+8{x}_{2}^{2} \\  & =5(0)^{2}+8(1)^{2} \\  & =8.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, given that $‖x‖=1,$ the maximum value of $Q(x)$ is equal to $8.$

$$
2{x}_{1}^{2}\le 4{x}_{1}^{2},\,-7{x}_{2}^{2}\le 4{x}_{2}^{2}.
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}Q(x) & =2{x}_{1}^{2}-7{x}_{2}^{2}+4{x}_{3}^{2} \\  & \le 4{x}_{1}^{2}+4{x}_{2}^{2}+4{x}_{3}^{2} \\  & =4({x}_{1}^{2}+{x}_{2}^{2}+{x}_{3}^{2}).\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}4({x}_{1}^{2}+{x}_{2}^{2}+{x}_{3}^{2})=4(1)=4.\end{aligned}
$$

and, in turn, $Q(x)\le 4.$

So, the value of $Q(x)$ can be no greater than $4.$ But before we conclude that $4$ is the maximum, we need to find a vector such that $Q(x)=4.$

$$
\begin{aligned}Q(x) & =2{x}_{1}^{2}-7{x}_{2}^{2}+4{x}_{3}^{2} \\  & =2(0)^{2}-7(0)^{2}+4(1)^{2} \\  & =4.\end{aligned}

$$

$$
4{x}_{1}^{2}\ge 2{x}_{1}^{2},\,3{x}_{2}^{2}\ge 2{x}_{2}^{2}.

$$
\begin{aligned}Q(x) & =4{x}_{1}^{2}+3{x}_{2}^{2}+2{x}_{3}^{2} \\  & \ge 2{x}_{1}^{2}+2{x}_{2}^{2}+2{x}_{3}^{2} \\  & =2({x}_{1}^{2}+{x}_{2}^{2}+{x}_{3}^{2}).\end{aligned}
$$

Now, recall that $‖x‖=1$ is equivalent to ${x}_{1}^{2}+{x}_{2}^{2}+{x}_{3}^{2}=1.$ So, 

$$
\begin{aligned}2({x}_{1}^{2}+{x}_{2}^{2}+{x}_{3}^{2})=2(1)=2.\end{aligned}
$$

and, in turn, $Q(x)\ge 2.$

$$

$$

after.problem: Find the minimum value of $Q(x)=4{x}_{1}^{2}-{x}_{2}^{2}-2{x}_{3}^{2}$ given that $‖x‖=1.$
after.worked_solution:
First, notice that ${x}_{1}^{2}\ge 0$ and ${x}_{2}^{2}\ge 0.$ So, we have that

$$
4{x}_{1}^{2}\ge -2{x}_{1}^{2},\,-{x}_{2}^{2}\ge -2{x}_{2}^{2}.
$$

As a result, 

$$
\begin{aligned}Q(x) & =4{x}_{1}^{2}-{x}_{2}^{2}-2{x}_{3}^{2} \\  & \ge -2{x}_{1}^{2}-2{x}_{2}^{2}-2{x}_{3}^{2} \\  & =-2({x}_{1}^{2}+{x}_{2}^{2}+{x}_{3}^{2}).\end{aligned}
$$

Now, recall that $‖x‖=1$ is equivalent to ${x}_{1}^{2}+{x}_{2}^{2}+{x}_{3}^{2}=1.$ So, 

$$
\begin{aligned}-2({x}_{1}^{2}+{x}_{2}^{2}+{x}_{3}^{2})=-2(1)=-2.\end{aligned}
$$

and, in turn, $Q(x)\ge -2.$ 

So, the value of $Q(x)$ can be no smaller than $-2.$ But before we conclude that $-2$ is the minimum, we need to find a vector such that $Q(x)=-2.$

Notice that when $x={[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}^{T},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}Q(x) & =4{x}_{1}^{2}-{x}_{2}^{2}-2{x}_{3}^{2} \\  & =4(0)^{2}-(0)^{2}-2(1)^{2} \\  & =-2.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, given that $‖x‖=1,$ the minimum value of $Q(x)$ is equal to $-2.$

after.name: Question 10
after.problem: Find the minimum value of $Q(x)=5{x}_{1}^{2}+3{x}_{2}^{2}$ given that $‖x‖=1.$
after.worked_solution:
First, notice that ${x}_{1}^{2}\ge 0.$ So, we have that

$$
5{x}_{1}^{2}\ge 3{x}_{1}^{2}.
$$

As a result, 

$$
\begin{aligned}Q(x) & =5{x}_{1}^{2}+3{x}_{2}^{2} \\  & \ge 3{x}_{1}^{2}+3{x}_{2}^{2} \\  & =3({x}_{1}^{2}+{x}_{2}^{2}).\end{aligned}
$$

Now, recall that $‖x‖=1$ is equivalent to ${x}_{1}^{2}+{x}_{2}^{2}=1.$ So, 

$$
\begin{aligned}3({x}_{1}^{2}+{x}_{2}^{2})=3(1)=3.\end{aligned}
$$

and, in turn, $Q(x)\ge 3.$ 

So, the value of $Q(x)$ can be no smaller than $3.$ But before we conclude that $3$ is the minimum, we need to find a vector such that $Q(x)=3.$

Notice that when  $x={[\begin{aligned}0 & 1\end{aligned}]}^{T},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}Q(x) & =5{x}_{1}^{2}+3{x}_{2}^{2} \\  & =5(0)+3(1)^{2} \\  & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, given that $‖x‖=1,$ the minimum value of $Q(x)$ is equal to $3.$

after.name: Question 11
after.problem: Find the maximum value of $Q(x)={x}_{1}^{2}+8{x}_{1}{x}_{2}+{x}_{2}^{2}$ given that $‖x‖=1.$
after.worked_solution:
Let $A$ be the matrix corresponding to our quadratic form. Recall that: 

- The maximum value of $Q(x),$ when $‖x‖=1,$ is equal to the largest eigenvalue of $A:$

$$
max{Q(x)\,|\,‖x‖=1}={\lambda }_{\text{max}}
$$

- The minimum value of $Q(x),$ when $‖x‖=1,$ is equal to the smallest eigenvalue of $A:$

$$
min{Q(x)\,|\,‖x‖=1}={\lambda }_{\text{min}}
$$

First, we write down the matrix of our quadratic form:

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 4 \\ 4 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

Now, we need to calculate the eigenvalues of the matrix $A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}|A-\lambda I| & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}1-\lambda  & 4 \\ 4 & 1-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (1-\lambda )(1-\lambda )-16 & =0 \\ {\lambda }^{2}-2\lambda -15 & =0 \\ (\lambda +3)(\lambda -5) & =0 \\ \lambda  & =-3,\,5\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
max{Q(x)\,|\,‖x‖=1}=5.
$$

after.name: Question 12
after.problem: Find the maximum value of $Q(x)=5{x}_{1}^{2}+4{x}_{1}{x}_{2}+5{x}_{2}^{2}$ given that $‖x‖=1.$
after.worked_solution:
Let $A$ be the matrix corresponding to our quadratic form. Recall that: 

- The maximum value of $Q(x),$ when $‖x‖=1,$ is equal to the largest eigenvalue of $A:$

$$
max{Q(x)\,|\,‖x‖=1}={\lambda }_{\text{max}}
$$

- The minimum value of $Q(x),$ when $‖x‖=1,$ is equal to the smallest eigenvalue of $A:$

$$
min{Q(x)\,|\,‖x‖=1}={\lambda }_{\text{min}}
$$

First, we write down the matrix of our quadratic form:

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}5 & 2 \\ 2 & 5\end{aligned}]
$$

Now, we need to calculate the eigenvalues of the matrix $A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}|A-\lambda I| & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}5-\lambda  & 2 \\ 2 & 5-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (5-\lambda )(5-\lambda )-4 & =0 \\ {\lambda }^{2}-10\lambda +21 & =0 \\ (\lambda -3)(\lambda -7) & =0 \\ \lambda  & =3,\,7\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
max{Q(x)\,|\,‖x‖=1}=7.
$$
